title: An effective global Langlands correspondence over number fields

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a usable mathematical dictionary between two ways of describing arithmetic over number fields, which are finite extensions of the rational numbers. Galois representations encode symmetries of algebraic equations through linear algebra. Automorphic representations encode highly structured analytic and representation-theoretic information. A global Langlands correspondence would identify appropriately matched objects on these two sides, allowing information expressed in one framework to be recovered in the other.

The intended scope is a correspondence in both directions for specified classes of reductive groups, together with local-global compatibility: the global match must agree with the relevant correspondences at each completion of the number field, including its infinite places. For general groups, the dictionary requires carefully defined arithmetic parameters, collections of representations called packets, and consistent normalizations. It cannot be formulated as an unrestricted pairing of arbitrary Galois representations with arbitrary automorphic data.

An additional proposed capability is effectivity. Once finite descriptions of admissible inputs and outputs have been specified, a proved terminating procedure would recover corresponding data in stated degrees and ranges. This algorithmic requirement is part of the innovation proposed here; the supplied sources do not establish that precise formulation. Effectivity would make the dictionary constructively usable, but termination alone would not guarantee computational practicality or polynomial running time.

significance.text: A sufficiently general correspondence would turn translations between arithmetic symmetry and automorphic analysis into a systematic method. The potential importance has a concrete precedent: Zhu identifies modularity of elliptic curves as a special case of the Langlands correspondence that implies Fermat’s Last Theorem. That example illustrates the reach of such connections without establishing that every future correspondence would produce consequences of comparable scale.

One specifically supported consequence is meromorphic continuation of the L-functions of general motives within the correspondence’s scope. Zhu explains that this would follow from the Galois-to-automorphic direction over number fields. Meromorphic continuation extends an L-function beyond its initial domain while allowing poles; it should not be replaced by an unqualified promise of holomorphic continuation or of all expected analytic properties.

Reciprocity supplies the central dictionary, while general functoriality concerns transfers of automorphic information between groups. A broadly useful theory would connect these capabilities, but a vaguely specified correspondence does not automatically prove every desired transfer. Functoriality therefore needs explicit hypotheses and results. Likewise, continuation of an L-function does not by itself establish finer relations between its central vanishing, algebraic cycles, Selmer groups, or arithmetic rank.

The Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture asks for finer arithmetic information about elliptic curves, including a relationship between rank and the behavior of an L-function at its central point. The proposed dictionary alone would not settle it. Possible applications to cryptography or physics would also require additional theorems and constructions; neither follows simply from a global number-field correspondence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability sought is a global number-field correspondence with explicitly matched arithmetic and automorphic classes, both directions, and compatibility at all places. Establishing isolated families is valuable, but does not establish the full general-group scope. Zhu’s account describes number-field Langlands as substantially more complicated than its function-field counterpart, including analytic difficulties and additional complications at places above the coefficient prime ℓ and at infinity.

A complete formulation must specify which arithmetic parameters are admissible, which automorphic representations match them, how packets are organized for general groups, and which normalizations make local and global constructions agree. These choices determine the theorem being sought. A one-direction construction of semisimple local parameters, for example, supplies important information without recovering the full global correspondence or the broader categorical structure.

The proposed effective version adds a separate mathematical and engineering barrier: represent the relevant objects finitely, define what counts as recovering a corresponding object or packet, and prove that the construction terminates throughout its claimed range. Practical use would additionally require bounds or measurements of computational cost. The supplied evidence provides neither an algorithm meeting these requirements nor a definitive algorithmic specification.

The geometric proof offers ideas rather than an automatic solution in another setting. Quanta’s July 2024 account reports Tony Feng’s warning that substantial parts would require serious adjustment for the number-theory and function-field settings. The retained geometric final paper concerns a categorical equivalence in a global, untwisted, unramified, de Rham setting; transporting that result to arithmetic over number fields requires further arguments.

current_state.text: The supplied review documents substantial established components: local Langlands for GL(n), Ngô’s fundamental lemma, and modularity’s connection to Fermat’s Last Theorem. These have different roles: a local correspondence, a result supporting comparison methods, and a major arithmetic example, respectively. They do not collectively establish the proposed effective global number-field dictionary. Class field theory is also identified in the supplied research as the abelian precedent, although the retained review does not independently document that identification in its asserted global scope.

Fargues and Scholze’s Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence, first posted in 2021 and identified in the supplied research with a 27 November 2024 revision, constructs continuous semisimple local L-parameters from irreducible smooth representations of a p-adic group. The retained review locates this construction in Proposition I.9.1 and distinguishes it from the broader categorical equivalence, which the paper states as a conjecture. This is a local construction in one direction, rather than the global effective correspondence proposed here.

Quanta reported on 19 July 2024 that the geometric Langlands proof extended over more than 800 pages across five papers. The retained final paper by Gaitsgory and Raskin was first submitted on 15 September 2024 and revised on 16 January 2026. Its introduction asserts the relevant categorical equivalence, and its scope is explicitly global, untwisted, unramified and de Rham. These dates distinguish the earlier public account from the later final-paper version; the supplied evidence does not establish a refereed publication status for the whole series.

Function-field arithmetic is a separate setting with substantial results of its own. Zhu’s survey discusses a global GL(n) theorem over function fields; that theorem must not be imported into number fields. Quanta’s July 2024 report separately describes work to translate the geometric proof into a function-field result as still in progress at that time. This was a dated report about a further translation, rather than a claim that function-field Langlands had no established theorems.

The evidence has material limits. According to the supplied review, the retained geometric final-paper extraction stops during page 58 of a longer document. The Fargues–Scholze extraction is also truncated, and some PDF pages have no extractable text. Their retained statements support the distinctions above, but do not amount to an independent assessment of the complete proofs. Zhu’s survey was posted on 10 April 2025 but reflects an ICM 2022 account, so its older geometric-conjecture language should be read in that historical context.

No retained source verifies the research’s claimed 19 October 2026 Institute for Advanced Study talk or the associated OpenAI manuscript on unramified function-field Langlands. That claim therefore cannot establish a further achievement here. The supplied materials also contain no freshness-search record establishing the precise number-field target’s status as of 1 November 2026. The documented results do not supply that target, but the absence of a current verification is not proof that no subsequent advance exists.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed major milestone: a refereed proof of the global correspondence for GL(n), for every n over every number field, with explicitly defined matching classes of arithmetic and automorphic objects, both directions, and local-global compatibility at every place. The scope must state all hypotheses and exclusions. This would be a major milestone rather than completion of the broader target for general reductive groups.
completion_criteria.label: Bidirectional GL(n) correspondence over every number field with local-global compatibility

completion_criteria.text: Proposed additional requirements: establish functorial transfer for at least one explicitly identified infinite family of classical groups beyond a precisely listed baseline of existing endoscopic results, and publish one new arithmetic theorem whose only remaining unproved hypothesis was the relevant correspondence. These are proposed demonstrations of scope and mathematical usefulness, not established community standards. Any claim to complete the general-group target would still require a theorem covering the full declared group classes.
completion_criteria.label: Beyond-baseline infinite-family classical-group transfer and a new arithmetic theorem

completion_criteria.text: To demonstrate effectivity, specify finite input and output formats and provide a proved terminating procedure for recovering corresponding data in each claimed direction over a stated range. Independent researchers should be able to reconstruct the procedure, verify its outputs against the theorem, and reproduce worked cases using different fields, degrees and local behavior. Resource requirements should be reported so that constructive existence can be distinguished from practical computation; no polynomial-time threshold is assumed.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible terminating bidirectional recovery procedures with reported resource requirements

completion_criteria.text: Convincing verification would combine scrutiny of the proof with reproducible constructions and explicit checks of local-global compatibility. Finite examples establish demonstrated breadth and can expose errors, but cannot establish literal universality; universal claims require proofs. A geometric theorem, a function-field theorem, or a proof of Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer alone would not meet these proposed number-field and effectivity criteria.
completion_criteria.label: Universal number-field claims proved, with reproducible constructions and compatibility checks

related_concepts.text: Class field theory, modularity of elliptic curves, local Langlands and Ngô’s fundamental lemma are related precedents or components, rather than interchangeable names for this innovation. The supplied research places class field theory as the abelian precedent, with the evidentiary qualification given above. Modularity illustrates a powerful special case; local Langlands concerns individual completions; the fundamental lemma supports comparison methods. Geometric Langlands and function-field Langlands share organizing ideas with the number-field program but concern distinct settings and theorems.

Roster comparison—MAT-01, Practical polynomial-time algorithms for NP-complete problems: both concepts seek broadly reusable capabilities, but MAT-02’s proposed terminating procedure makes no polynomial-time claim and supplies no general method for NP-complete problems. MAT-05, Research-scale machine-checked mathematical discovery, could help formalize or check a Langlands proof or construction. Formal verification and automated discovery are separate capabilities from establishing this particular correspondence.

Roster comparison—MAT-06, Classical polynomial-time integer factorization and discrete logarithms, and MAT-09, Classical polynomial-time algorithms for cryptographic lattice problems: all have connections to number theory or arithmetic computation, but the supplied evidence gives no reduction from an effective Langlands dictionary to these algorithms. A terminating correspondence procedure would not by itself establish practical attacks on those cryptographic problems.

Roster comparison—MAT-03, A first-principles theory of turbulent transport, and MAT-04, Proved polynomial-cost solution of high-dimensional nonlinear PDEs: these concern physical transport and computational solution of equations. Langlands has an analytic side, but that shared mathematical vocabulary does not supply either capability. MAT-08, Polynomial-time chemical accuracy for molecular electronic structure, likewise requires a separate computational breakthrough; the proposed arithmetic dictionary does not establish molecular simulation accuracy or cost bounds.

Roster comparison—MAT-07, A prescriptive mathematical theory of deep learning: both seek a theory that supports systematic reasoning, but their objects and success criteria differ. A Langlands correspondence would connect specified arithmetic and automorphic structures, whereas MAT-07 concerns predictive guidance for learning systems. No implication between the two innovations is established by the supplied materials.

brief.title: A usable dictionary for the mathematics of equations
possible: Mathematicians studying equations could move between descriptions of their symmetries and special analytic patterns called automorphic representations. The dictionary would work over number fields: number systems that extend the rational numbers by a finite amount.

They could also use procedures guaranteed to finish to recover a matching description in either direction. The match would cover specified families of symmetry groups and agree with descriptions obtained by examining the number field locally.
why: This would give number theorists a systematic way to bring tools from different branches of mathematics to the same problem. A special case of this kind of connection already underlies the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem.

sources.showed: Zhu surveys connections between geometry and arithmetic, including established correspondences in related settings and applications to problems about equations.
sources.quote:
A special case of this correspondence, known as the Shimura-Tanniyama-Weil conjecture, implies

sources.cited_for: Special cases demonstrate how translating between mathematical descriptions can yield arithmetic theorems.
sources.not_established: The survey does not establish a general dictionary over number fields or terminating procedures for using it.

milestones.explanation: Procedures with finite inputs and outputs must provably finish in both directions over stated ranges, with independent reproduction of varied examples and reported resource needs. This makes the dictionary constructively usable.

page.title: Global Langlands reciprocity for GL(n) over number fields
page.definition: Over each number field F, a finite extension of Q, the conjecture pairs two kinds of representation. On one side are irreducible n-dimensional ℓ-adic linear actions of the symmetries of an algebraic closure of F. These actions are geometric: they are unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at every prime above ℓ. On the other side are algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations, generated by cusp forms on GL(n) over the adeles of F. The pairing would be a bijection in every dimension, with matching local parameters at each finite and infinite place.

goal.need: For an abelian variety over a number field, point counts over finite fields give an Euler product for its L-function that converges absolutely for Re(s) > 3/2. The arithmetic question concerns s = 1. Matching the local factors with automorphic ones would extend the L-function to that point and give meaning to its order of vanishing. Whether that order equals the rank of the group of rational points is a separate conjecture. The same method would give meromorphic continuation for motivic L-functions more generally.

completion.title: Both directions of GL(n) reciprocity hold over every number field, with compatibility at all places.
completion.criterion: For every number field F, n ≥ 1, prime ℓ and isomorphism ι from an algebraic closure of Qℓ to C, prove a bijection up to isomorphism between irreducible geometric n-dimensional ℓ-adic Galois representations ρ and algebraic cuspidal π on GLₙ(A_F). At each finite v, ι WD(ρ|G_Fᵥ)ᶠ⁻ˢˢ must equal recᵥ(πᵥ ⊗ |det|ᵥ^((1−n)/2)) up to isomorphism, including the monodromy operator. At v above ℓ use Fontaine’s D_pst. At infinity require Harris’s archimedean parameters from the labeled Hodge–Tate data and, at real places, complex conjugation.
completion.set_by: The GL(n) reciprocity conjecture, in Harris’s Conjecture 1.1 and the finite-place normalization of Thorne’s Conjecture 2.5.
completion.threshold_quote: Then there is a unique bijection between the following two sets of objects:
completion.basis: Thorne gives the normalized comparison at every finite place. Harris also specifies the archimedean local components.

milestones.title: One-dimensional finite-image Galois representations match Hecke characters over every number field.
milestones.criterion: For every finite abelian extension L/F of number fields, the global Artin map induces C_F/N_{L/F}(C_L) ≅ Gal(L/F). Here C_F is the restricted product of the groups Fᵥ×, with respect to the local unit groups at finite places, modulo the diagonally embedded F×. Taking characters gives a bijection between finite-image one-dimensional Galois representations and finite-order Hecke characters, compatible with local reciprocity.
milestones.set_by: Artin reciprocity, a field convention stated in Milne’s Class Field Theory, Chapter V, Theorem 5.3 and Remark 5.7.
milestones.threshold_quote: For every finite abelian extension L of K, the Artin map defines an isomorphism

milestones.title: Every elliptic curve over Q is modular.
milestones.criterion: For every elliptic curve E over Q of conductor N, there is a weight-2 cuspidal newform f of level N with L(E,s) = L(f,s). Equivalently, for each prime ℓ the representation on the ℓ-adic Tate module of E, after extension of scalars, is the Galois representation attached to f.
milestones.set_by: The modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over Q, established as Theorem A by Breuil, Conrad, Diamond and Taylor. This threshold concerns the elliptic-curve case over Q.
milestones.threshold_quote: for some eigenform f of weight 2 and level N(E).

milestones.title: Regular algebraic GL(n) cusp forms over CM or totally real fields have matching Galois representations.
milestones.criterion: Let F be CM or totally real, n ≥ 1, π a regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GLₙ(A_F), and ι an isomorphism from an algebraic closure of Qℓ to C. There is a unique continuous semisimple n-dimensional ℓ-adic representation r up to isomorphism with the following property. At each v above a rational prime q ≠ ℓ at which π is unramified at every place above q, r is unramified and ι(r|W_Fᵥ)ˢˢ ≅ recᵥ(πᵥ ⊗ |det|ᵥ^((1−n)/2)). Regular algebraic means that π at infinity has the infinitesimal character of an irreducible algebraic representation.
milestones.set_by: Harris, Lan, Taylor and Thorne, Theorem A of On the rigid cohomology of certain Shimura varieties; the threshold is restricted to regular algebraic representations over CM or totally real fields.
milestones.threshold_quote: Then there is a unique continuous semi-simple representation

milestones.title: Every L-algebraic cuspidal GL(n) representation over a number field has an associated Galois representation.
milestones.criterion: For every number field F, n ≥ 1, prime ℓ and L-algebraic cuspidal π on GLₙ(A_F), fix an identification of complex and ℓ-adic coefficients. Require a continuous n-dimensional ℓ-adic Galois representation matching the unramified Weil parameter at every unramified finite place away from ℓ. At every v above ℓ it is de Rham with the Hodge–Tate cocharacter of Remark 3.2.3, and crystalline if πᵥ is unramified. At each real place its complex-conjugation class is the one specified in Lemma 2.3.2.
milestones.set_by: Buzzard and Gee, Conjecture 3.2.2, restricted here to GL(n); this is the automorphic-to-Galois direction.
milestones.threshold_quote: Then there is a continuous Galois representation

milestones.title: Over CM fields, regular algebraic cusp forms match de Rham parameters above ℓ up to semisimplification.
milestones.criterion: For every CM field F, n ≥ 1, prime ℓ, coefficient isomorphism ι and regular algebraic cuspidal π on GLₙ(A_F) of weight λ, let r be the associated ℓ-adic representation. For every v above ℓ, r|G_Fᵥ is de Rham. At each embedding τ inducing v its Hodge–Tate weights are the multiset {λ_{ιτ,i}+n−i : 1 ≤ i ≤ n}. The semisimplification of WD(r|G_Fᵥ) agrees via ι with the semisimplification of the Tate-normalized local Langlands parameter of πᵥ.
milestones.set_by: A’Campo, Hevesi, Thorne and Whitmore, Conjecture 1.1.3(2) and Theorem 1.2.1.

milestones.title: Over CM or totally real fields, regular algebraic cusp forms match locally up to semisimplification away from ℓ.
milestones.criterion: For every CM or totally real field F, n ≥ 1, prime ℓ, coefficient isomorphism ι and regular algebraic cuspidal π on GLₙ(A_F), let r be its associated ℓ-adic representation. For every finite v not dividing ℓ, including those where π or F is ramified, require ι WD(r|G_Fᵥ)ˢˢ ≅ recᵥ(πᵥ ⊗ |det|ᵥ^((1−n)/2))ˢˢ. Here semisimplification compares the underlying semisimple Weil representations.
milestones.set_by: Ila Varma, Theorem 1 of Local-global compatibility for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations when ℓ ≠ p.
milestones.threshold_quote: we extend local-global compatibility up to semisimplification (1.1) to all primes

milestones.title: Every irreducible geometric ℓ-adic Galois representation over a number field is cuspidal automorphic.
milestones.criterion: For every number field F, n ≥ 1, prime ℓ and coefficient isomorphism, start with an irreducible continuous n-dimensional ℓ-adic representation ρ of the absolute Galois group of F. Assume ρ is unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham above ℓ. Form Π(ρ) from its prescribed local components at all places as in Harris’s Conjecture 1.1(a). Require Π(ρ) to occur in the space of cusp forms on GLₙ(F)\GLₙ(A_F), with the prescribed algebraicity at infinity.
milestones.set_by: The Galois-to-automorphic direction of Langlands reciprocity, Harris’s Conjecture 1.1(a).

definition = "Over each number field F, a finite extension of Q, the conjecture pairs two kinds of representation. On one side are irreducible n-dimensional \u2113-adic linear actions of the symmetries of an algebraic closure of F. These actions are geometric: they are unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at every prime above \u2113. On the other side are algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations, generated by cusp forms on GL(n) over the adeles of F. The pairing would be a bijection in every dimension, with matching local parameters at each finite and infinite place.". Reason: The definition omits irreducibility and states the conjectured matches as an established fact.

goal.need = "For an abelian variety over a number field, point counts over finite fields give an Euler product for its L-function that converges absolutely for Re(s) > 3/2. The arithmetic question concerns s = 1. Matching the local factors with automorphic ones would extend the L-function to that point and give meaning to its order of vanishing. Whether that order equals the rank of the group of rational points is a separate conjecture. The same method would give meromorphic continuation for motivic L-functions more generally.". Reason: The existing text names analytic continuation without explaining which arithmetic question needs values outside the original region of convergence.
